newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Technicals turn sloppy in US debt futures.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Technicals turn sloppy in US debt futures.

text.p: Technicals turned sloppy in the U.S. debt futures market, but analysts said it was too early in the day to determine whether September T-bonds would stage a reversal from their seven-month highs.
"It certainly represents a potential reversal day, but it's too early to tell," said Richard Scarlata, editor and publisher of the Sutton Daily Advisory Letter.

September T-bonds set a daily low at 113-23/32 after rising to 114-09/32, a fresh seven-month high, in a knee-jerk reaction to the U.S. June Producer Price Index. PPI fell 0.1 percent, versus estimates of unchanged.
"It's a negative that we had six months of consecutive declines in PPI and yet we turned unchanged and down a tick," Scarlata said.
He and other traders said September T-bonds would have to fall below 113-16/32, which was Thursday's pit low, to set a reversal.

The contract fell through the pivot point at 113-24/32, reducing the likelihood for September to test resistance at 114-16/32, which currently corresponds to the key 6.50 percent yield level in U.S. cash bonds, they said. Some were eyeing 114-22/32, an Elliott Wave objective, as near-term resistance.
September T-bonds are now closer to near-term support of 113-22/32. Traders pegged further support at 113-12/32 to 113-11/32.
"It's disturbing because those people who bought early aren't backing it up with more buying," a T-bond futures analyst said.

He said today's pit action could be a precursor to declines next week. He anticipates September T-bonds falling through last Thursday's closing price of 113-06/32 early next week. Despite the early rally in September bonds and December Eurodollars, traders were cautious ahead of today's opening.
They noted diverging daily momentum indicators following Thursday's price action, as well as overbought conditions. Scarlata said his market condition index still showed overbought conditions.
Another debt market analyst said December Eurodollars had finished their 12th week of gains, as the 13th week usually was a retracement period.

Even though December Eurodollars re-tested Wednesday's high of 94.09, their highest level since February 20, the contract failed to rise above its 200-day moving average of about 94.25 on a weekly continuation chart, the analyst said.
He also noted that December remains below its 50-month moving average of about 94.50 on a continuation chart.
"I'm thinking that this rally was a countertrend and that the market could be rolling over into a downtrend," he said.
September two-year T-notes were vulnerable to dipping below their 200-day moving average at 103-08/32, he said.

"We aren't that far above that level," he said. "We were above it in the fourth quarter of 1996 and first quarter of 1997, but now it's a question of whether we can hold above that level in the next month or two."
